title: Instructions
body:
The Documize Community edition repositiory is: https://github.com/documize/community

Although the Documize binaries run on Linux, Windows and macOS, the build process has only been tested on macOS.

Install the prerequisites:

  • Go from https://golang.org (be careful to set the $GOPATH environment variable correctly, you may find https://www.goinggo.net/2016/05/installing-go-and-your-workspace.html helpful)
  • Node (v4.4.5 LTS+) from https://nodejs.org/
  • NPM from https://www.npmjs.com 
  • Ember from http://emberjs.com/ 
  • Bower from https://bower.io/
  • MySQL (v5.7.10+) from http://dev.mysql.com/downloads/mysql/ (don't forget to copy the one-time password and your system may require a restart)

Make sure this repository sits at the following position relative to your $GOPATH: $GOPATH/src/github.com/documize/community

After cloning the repository in the above location, go there and run:

cd gui
npm install
cd ..
./build.sh 

The build script packages up the Ember JS/HTML/CSS code for production use, then generates Go code that creates a simple in-memory file system to contain it. That generated Go code is compiled with the rest to produce a single binary for each of the target systems. 

Your ./bin directory should now contain a set of binaries for a number of target systems. This binary can be executed on any system which also has access to a MySQL database with no further dependencies.

Use a MySQL tool (like MySQLWorkbench) to create an empty database for Documize to use, making sure that the default collation setting is utf8_general_ci or some other utf8 variant. For advice on how to configure your MySQL server, see this guide.

Run Documize for the first time to set-up the database and your user information (for example on OSX, using port 5001, MySQL user root/password and database ‘documize’):

./bin/documize-darwin-amd64 -port=5001 -db='root:password@tcp(localhost:3306)/documize'

An error message will appear in the log to say your installation is in set-up mode. Now navigate to http://localhost:5001 and follow the instructions.

Hopefully you will now have a working Documize instance.

Now make a note of the "salt" value given in the log and make sure you provide it as a runtime parameter (-salt=???) or set the environment variable DOCUMIZESALT for all future invocations. For more runtime options, please see the Configure Documize guide.

Once you have set-up the database as described above, you could go to the ./documize directory and use the command "go run documize.go" in place of the binary name.

title: Ember
body:
This section is only required if you want to develop the Ember code.

These two commands are best run in different terminal windows: 

(1) Run the Go binary needs to run an SSL server on port 5001 (see instructions in the Documize configuration guide).

(2) Run the Ember code using the command "ember s" from the gui directory.

Ember should be visible by navigating to http://localhost:4200

title: Contributing
body:
Thank you for your interest in contributing to Documize.

Documize is provided in two ways:

  1. Documize Community Edition (CE) our free and open source edition, and;
  2. Documize Enterprise Edition (EE) our commercial edition.

You may see these two products abbreviated as CE and EE.

title: Security Vulnerability Disclosure
body:
In the first instance please report any suspected or confirmed security vulnerabilities to security@documize.com

Please give us reasonable time to respond before making any information about the security issue public.

Do not disclose publically, create an issue in our public issue tracker.

title: Introduction
body:
The export API provides the means to export documents.

  • [POST] /api/export

The POST body is a JSON payload detailing what should be exported:

{
    "filterType": "space",
    "spaceId": "some_id",
    "data": ["id_1", "id_2"]
}

The filterType can as follows:

  • space
  • category
  • document

The data field is a collection of string based object ID's -- space, category or document ID's.

When exporting category or document types, the spaceId value should be set to the space containing the categories or documents.

Exporting all documents from a single space:

{
    "filterType": "space",
    "spaceId": "",
    "data": ["id_1"]
}

 

Exporting all documents from multiple spaces:

{
    "filterType": "space",
    "spaceId": "",
    "data": ["id_1", "id_2"]
}

 

Exporting all documents assigned to categories in specified space:

{
    "filterType": "category",
    "spaceId": "space_1",
    "data": ["id_1", "id_2"]
}

 

Exporting specific documents in specified space:

{
    "filterType": "document",
    "spaceId": "space_1",
    "data": ["id_1", "id_2"]
}

title: User & Group Filters
body:
Filters are used to restrict the sub-set of users to pull from LDAP.

If you specify both user and group filters, then results from both queries will be merged and used.

Some examples of group filters:

(&(objectClass=group)(|(cn=ship_crew)(cn=admin_staff)))
(|(cn=Accounting)(cn=IT))
(|(ou=mathematicians)(ou=chemists))

Some examples of user filters:

(|(objectClass=person)(objectClass=user)(objectClass=inetOrgPerson))

title: Cloud vs. Self-host
body:
Documize is available as cloud-based service with instant sign-up and activation (software-as-a-service). Activation of the cloud service provides a dedicated URL for your business by allowing you to specify a subdomain. You can sign up for the cloud service from here:

https://documize.com/welcome

For those businesses that require a solution to be deployed behind the corporate firewall, Documize can be downloaded and installed as a self-hosted application. You can download the binary relevant to your OS from here:

https://documize.com/downloads

In terms of upgrading your self-hosted installation of Documize, the process is dead simple as per the instructions.

title: Self-host Prerequisites
body:
To self-host Documize, you need the following:

  1. Windows, Linux or macOS operating system
  2. PostgreSQL, MySQL, Percona or MariaDB database

That's it.

The downloadable Documize binary is not an installer -- it is the actual product.

In terms of the Documize technology stack, we use:

  • EmberJS as the front-end framework
  • Golang as the server-side environment (not Java/Ruby/PHP/Dotnet)

Thanks to Golang, there are ZERO runtime dependencies. Documize ships as a self-contained executable which includes a web server.

Read the Documize Installation Guide

title: Introduction
body:
Documize takes a different approach towards producing, sharing and tracking documentation.

The difference is more than product capabilities -- the underlying business and engineering philosophy impacts how you license, install and maintain Documize.

The Documize difference means less work for IT professionals in terms of product deployment and subsequent up-keep.

title: Introduction
body:
Documize can delegate user authentication to Keycloak thereby enabling LDAP, AD integration.

This document assumes that the Documize administrator has installed and is familiar with Keycloak server.

http://www.keycloak.org

Documize is tested against the Keyclok version 2.5.5 final.

title: Service Account
body:
Documize requires a "service account" to sync users with Documize. This user account should be created in the Master Realm

This account should be created in the Master realm and be given the view-users role.

Note: the manage-users role should be assigned against the Realm being used by Documize.

title: Realm
body:
You can either use an existing Realm or create one for use by Documize.

Public Key

You will need to copy the RSA Public Key as Documize uses this key to verify signatures of tokens generated by Keycloak.

Click the Public Key button to the right of the RSA entry (first row in below screenshot). Then copy the Public Key for later use within Documize.

Tokens

Configure token timeout settings.

title: Client
body:
Create a Client within the chosen Realm that will be used by Documize.

Settings

Use the following settings to configure the Client -- note the Client Protocol, Access Type, Standard Flow and Direct Access Grants.

 

The URL endpoints should be configured to reflect both Keycloak and Documize URLs.

Ensure Web Origins has the "*" entry as above.

Mappers

Four fields are required by Documize.

These fields are expected to be named as follows in the JWT response -- note the casing:

  • username
  • lastName
  • firstName
  • email

title: Configuring Documize
body:
Keycloak authentication is configured and enabled from Settings.

Type in the Keycloak Server URL, Realm name, Client name, RSA Public Key, Documize Service account details.

Clicking the Save button will redirect you to login via Keycloak.

title: Overview
body:
Documize is a fully multi-tenanted application capable of serving multiple separated customers from within the same running instance.

A single Documize installation supports multiple tenants and identifies different tenants based upon URL.

  • https://legal.example.org
  • https://finance.example.org
  • https://tech.example.org

A Documize user can have access to one or more tenants.

Each tenants data is protected from the other tenants.

title: Technical Structure
body:
There are two levels of Administrator within Documize.

  • Global administrator -- can manage settings affecting all tenants and data.
  • Tenant administrator -- can manage settings affecting only their data.

 

From the above list of settings, the following can only be managed by a Global Administrator:

  • Mail Server
  • Authentication
  • Audit Log
  • Billing

So who gets access to global configuration? Anyone who is marked as such in the dmz_user table (set during initial installation setup wizard).

Tenant Administrators are marked as such in the dmz_account table.

The database schema represents tenants as follows:

  • dmz_org -- represents a Documize tenant (e.g. https://legal.domain.com)
  • dmz_user -- represents a Documize user
  • dmz_account -- maps Documize user to a Documize tenant

title: Introduction
body:
Documize utilizes your mail server for sending email notifications during the following scenarios:

  • New user sign-up
  • Password reset process
  • When someone is assigned an action
  • When someone shares content with others

Therefore, it is vital that you configure the mail server immediately after installing Documize.

title: Specify Host Address
body:
Usually you will provide either a fully qualified domain name or an IP address, and the SMTP port number.

Ensure the correct port number is being used and is not blocked from the machine hosting your Documize instance.

title: Introduction
body:
General options provide the means to customize Documize.

 

These options apply per tenant (in a multi-tenant deployment).

title: Site Meta
body:
What can be changed:

Site title and message can be customized:

The color scheme can be selected and applies to all users:

Optionally, upload a small logo that is rendered on the Documize home page.

title: Anonymous Access
body: By allowing anonymous access, anyone who navigates to the Documize instance can view any document within Everyone spaces. This is particularly useful in public-facing "wiki-style" scenarios.

title: Adding Users
body:
A user represents someone who needs to login and use Documize.

Users can be added one by one or bulk uploaded using a CSV file.

Adding a single user requires three inputs: first name, last name and their email address.

After a new user is added, they will receive a welcome email with the a link to Documize. They will be assigned a random password which they can change after logging into Documize.

You can also upload and create multiple users with a comma-delimited list of users.

All new users will receive a welcome email and assigned a random password.

title: Conversion Service Endpoint
body:
By default the following endpoint is used to handle Word document import and PDF generation: https://api.documize.com

This service can optionally be self-hosted by running this Docker container:

https://hub.docker.com/r/documize/conversion

When self-hosting this service, change the URL to point towards your Docker container (e.g. https://localhost:5010).

title: Introduction
body:
Search API provides the means to find content.

The endpoints for search:

  • POST /api/search — search content

The POST body consists of the following:

  • keywords —a OR b, x AND y, "phrase mat*"
  • content — search against document content?
  • doc — search against document title?
  • tag — search against document tag names?
  • attachment — search against document attachment names?

title: Introduction
body:
Users are assigned permissions to Spaces and Documents.

The endpoints for users:

  • POST /api/users — add user
  • GET /api/users — get all users
  • DELETE /api/user/{id} — delete user

The endpoints for user group membership:

  • GET /api/group — get list of user groups
  • POST /api/group/{groupId}/join/userId} — add user to group
  • DELETE /api/group/{groupId}/leave/userId} — remove user from group

These endpoints can only be invoked by users with Documize administrator rights.

In terms of payload, the following permissions should be noted:

  1. "editor" — can a user create spaces?
  2. "analytics" — can a user view insights and reports?
  3. "viewUsers" — can a user view lists of other users?

The "viewUsers" permission should be set to FALSE for external users that should not see names of internal employees.

Those users will have attributes such as first name, last name, email, etc.

  1. Unique ID value

  3. Last name (e.g. Smith)
  4. Email (e.g. john.smith@example.org)

Different LDAP compliant servers can name those user attributes differently.

If you have specified a Group Filter, you will need to specify the attribute name that specifies an individual group member.

title: Introduction
body:
The Documize API provides secure access to your data held. 

Create and fetch spaces and content from any programming language using the RESTful API.

The API follows the REST convention in terms of HTTP verbs:

  • Use HTTP GET to fetch data
  • Use HTTP POST to save new data
  • Use HTTP PUT to save existing data
  • Use HTTP DELETE to remove existing data

Documize does not use the HTTP PATCH verb to update attributes of existing data -- HTTP PUT is utilized for all data update operations.

For all API calls the HTTP request and response body format is JSON (application/json).

title: Request
body:
1. Prepare

The authentication process accepts Base64 encoded string that contains three elements, separated by a colon:

domain:email:password

Each of these parts is string value:

  1. domain: usually an empty string if you are running a single tenant Documize instance (which is normal for self-hosted installations).
  2. email: the email address of the user wanting to use the API (best practice is to create a dedicated "API" user within Documize).
  3. password: the password of the user wanting to use the API. 

As an example the string ":api@example.org:test" would result in a Base64 value of "OmFwaUBleGFtcGxlLm9yZzp0ZXN0".

For cloud instances of Documize hosted by us, should specify your sub-domain in the first part of the string. For example, if you login at https://docs.documize.com then the string would look like as follows:

docs:api@example.org:testpassword

This would result in as Base64 string of "ZG9jczphcGlAZXhhbXBsZS5vcmc6dGVzdHBhc3N3b3Jk".

 

2. Authenticate

The Base64 string is then passed to the authentication endpoint which will check supplied credentials and provide an outcome. The endpoint is located at:

# endpoint location

/api/public/authenticate

# self-host example

http://my-documize-server/api/public/authenticate

# cloud hosted (replace my-team with your sub-domain)

https://my-team.documize.com/api/public/authenticate

The endpoint expects a POST request with an Authorization header, as follows:

# HTTP header

Authorization   Basic <my-base-64-string>

# e.g. user 'api@example.org' logging onto 'https://docs.documize.com' with password of 'test'

Authorization   Basic ZG9jczphcGlAZXhhbXBsZS5vcmc6dGVzdHBhc3N3b3Jk

Note the space between 'Basic' and the Base64 encoded string.

title: Authentication
body:
All methods are authenticated and require valid user credentials. 

You make a POST request and then store the response for subsequent API calls (JWT).

title: Response
body:
If the authentication request succeeds, a JSON payload is returned that describes the user and associated permissions.

At the top level, the response object (JSON format) returns:

  1. The Authorization token to be supplied in all future API calls.
  2. The User object providing:
    1. User details
    2. Global permissions
    3. Account permissions

The permissions are split by Global and Account level to support multi-tenanted deployments where the same user has different permissions for two Documize accounts (e.g. tech.documize.com and finance.documize.com).

The token format is JWT compliant:

eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJkb21haW4iOiJkZW1vIiwiZXhwIjoxNTU1NDg5Mjg0LCJpc3MiOiJEb2N1bWl6ZSIsIm9yZyI6IjRUZWMzNHc4Iiwic3ViIjoid2ViYXBwIiwidXNlciI6Ild0V2tVcUlGc0xYcmxzMmQifQ.hIJZYH9O4g_fSjotDMJW6eCT0tq8QRZzsb2jEF_5ics

For all subsequent API calls, the token must be supplied again as Authorization Bearer header.

# HTTP header

Authorization   Bearer <token>

# e.g. 

Authorization   Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJkb21haW4iOiJkZW1vIiwiZXhwIjoxNTU1NDg5Mjg0LCJpc3MiOiJEb2N1bWl6ZSIsIm9yZyI6IjRUZWMzNHc4Iiwic3ViIjoid2ViYXBwIiwidXNlciI6Ild0V2tVcUlGc0xYcmxzMmQifQ.hIJZYH9O4g_fSjotDMJW6eCT0tq8QRZzsb2jEF_5ics

title: Introduction
body:
A document contains content, comments, attachments, versions, history, actions and more besides.

Therefore the API for documents provides granular access to the different parts of a document.

The endpoints for document structure:

  • GET /api/documents?space={id} — get documents list for space
  • GET /api/documents/{id} — get specified document (not content)
  • PUT /api/documents/{id} — update document title/excerpt
  • DELETE /api/documents/{id} — delete document 

The document endpoints provide the document name, excerpt and other metadata such as document lifecycle.

The endpoints for document content:

  • GET /api/documents/{id}/pages — get all content for document
  • GET /api/documents/{id}/pages/{id} — get specific content

Document content contains the HTML necessary to display the content.

By default Documize utilizes email and password combination for user authentication stored within the Documize database.

For large deployments, it is recommended that user account setup and authentication be off-loaded to your existing LDAP compliant server.

Active Directory (AD) is a directory service made by Microsoft. It provides functionality like authentication, group and user management, policy administration and more. LDAP is a way of speaking to Active Directory.

LDAP, which stands for Lightweight Directory Access Protocol, is a means for querying items in any directory service that supports it.

Documize is a free alternative to Atlassian Confluence that integrates with Atlassian Jira. This integration allows Jira issues to be displayed inside documentation.

If content stored within the Documize database is changed directly, then you should periodically rebuild the search index.

It can take between a few minutes and up to 30 minutes to rebuild the search index. During this time you can continue to use Documize as normal.

title: Introduction
body:
Documize is a multi-tenanted application enabling both "tech.mycompany.com" and "sales.mycompany.com" to run using the same executable/database.

All data is stored within the Documize database including attachments, images, settings, users, permissions. Nothing is stored on the file system containing the Documize binary executable.

The backup file is a compressed ZIP format file containing JSON format files per database table.

Each JSON file contains all data for the underlying database table.

The backup and restore process can be used to move between different database providers. For example, you can migrate between the current MySQL database to an empty PostgreSQL database. Contact support@documize.com for details.

title: Backup
body:
Depending upon the size of the database being used by Documize, It can take several minutes to complete the backup process.

Once the backup process is complete, the resultant ZIP will be automatically downloaded by the web browser.

Check the retain option if you want to also store the backup ZIP file on the server.

Each zip file is uniquely named:

Depending on your Documize installation type and permissions, you can perform a backup in either one or two ways:

  • BACKUP TENANT: for cloud-hosted customers the Documize administrator can login to perform a tenant-level backup (e.g. my-company.documize.com).
  • BACKUP SYSTEM: For self-hosting customers, the Documize global administrator can perform a complete system-wide backup across all tenants.

title: Restore
body:
Restoring from an existing backup will re-create users, groups, permissions, spaces, categories and all content.

For self-host customers, a system backup should only be restored to an empty/new database. A system restore will recreate all existing ID values.

title: Steps
body:
For the self-host option, the following represents the process for applying the latest product release on your server:
  1. Download the correct binary for your OS (Windows, Linux, macOS).
  2. Stop your existing Documize instance.
  3. Replace your existing binary with the newly downloaded binary.
  4. Start Documize again.
  5. That's it.

Documize will self-migrate the SQL database with any schema changes introduced in the new release.

Some points of interest:

  • You don't need to upgrade in sequence so feel free to jump from v1.60.0 to v1.65.0 (for example).
  • The process works in a clustered, multi-machine environments as well as single machine deployments -- the migration process automatically elects a leader to perform the database upgrade process.
  • The Documize cloud/SaaS offering uses the same binary that you install on your servers so we dog-food the process each time there is a new release.
  • We release updates frequently, usually twice a month. Documize administrators automatically receive an in-app notification about the latest product update. You will presented with a change summary for the new update.
  • Post-upgrade, regular Documize users receive a "What's New" message providing a friendly introduction to any changes and new features.

The upgrade process usually only takes a few minutes from start to finish.

title: Open Source Core & Product Editions
body:
Documize has an open source core so anyone can contribute changes to the core product framework.

By keeping the core of the product open source, individuals and companies can add new backend database storage providers, new authentication providers and most importantly, new integrations.

We believe that products should not implement walled gardens or marketplaces that charge extra for connecting third party systems to Documize. Marketplaces in particular can shield the true cost of a product when key functionality is packaged and sold by other vendors. Documize enables anyone to develop integrations to sync data with other systems.

The open source core is packaged and promoted as Documize Community Edition (CE). This is available for download and usage from GitHub.

https://github.com/documize/community

It's free to use for unlimited users for both personal and business use.

The open core platform is used by our flagship offering -- Documize Enterprise Edition (EE).

EE provides key capabilities required to drive the serious business of managing product documentation and other documents within demanding business scenarios.

EE is available for free download from Documize.com:

https://www.documize.com/downloads

title: Introduction
body:
Data integrations pull and embed data within Documize by connecting to third party systems.

A major differentiator for Documize is that all data integrations are open sourced on GitHub.

There are no marketplace fees, vendor walled gardens -- anyone can improve existing integrations or add new integrations.

It is assumed that software developers will be building new data integrations and have cloned the Community Edition code.

https://github.com/documize/community

title: Architecture
body:
Data integration development consists of two logic parts:

  1. The backend implementation built with Go
  2. The user interface, built with HMTL, CSS and Javascript (via EmberJS)

The user interface consists of two components that make up the user experience:

  1. Editing -- how users create and edit a section type
  2. Rendering -- how to render the result

The editing user interface component can either be inlined (e.g. Rich Text section) or full paged (e.g. Trello section). A full page section type is useful when you need to redirect to another service to complete an authorization flow, or require a wider canvas.

The recommended approach is to first implement the skeleton backend implementation followed by the user interface components.

The data that is generated by a section is held both in its raw form and the resultant HTML form that is displayed inside a document.

As an example, let's look at the Markdown section type:

  • the section type stores the markdown text as entered by users via markdown/type-editor.hbs & markdown/type-editor.js
  • the markdown.go file handles the conversion from markdown to HTML via markdown/markdown.go
  • the generate HTML is rendered on-screen via markdown/type-renderer.hbs and markdown/type-renderer.js

The database will hold the raw input and the resultant HTML.

All section data is stored within the database being used by Documize.

The logic to load and save section specific data is handled by Documize automatically.

For reference, note the the key tables and fields:

  • dmz_section contains the section data as HTML (c_rawbody)
  • dmz_section_meta contains section configuration and raw data (c_body)

The conversion from raw input to HTML is invoked by Documize each time a section edit is saved.

title: Backend
body:
Documize is built with Go -- it's an open source cross platform programming language designed by Google.

Backend code is located within this package:

https://github.com/documize/community/tree/master/domain/section

As a reference point, we will be using the existing Markdown section type as the basis for our new integration walkthrough.

The configuration meta for this section type is defined as follows:

// Meta describes us
func (*Provider) Meta() provider.TypeMeta {
	section := provider.TypeMeta{}

	section.ID = "1470bb4a-36c6-4a98-a443-096f5658378b"
	section.Title = "Markdown"
	section.Description = "CommonMark based content"
	section.ContentType = "markdown"
	section.PageType = "section"
	section.Order = 9998

	return section
}

Explanations for above section meta definition:

  • ID value is a UUID unique to this section type -- example https://www.uuidgenerator.net
  • Title & Description is how the section type is referenced on-screen
  • ContentType is a short unique textual label that is stored in the dmz_section.c_contenttype database field
  • PageType should be set to section for inline editing experience or tab for full page editing experience
  • Order defines where this section appears in the list of sections presented to the user

Each section requires three methods to be implemented:

  • Command -- (optional) used by section user interface components to access backend logic (see Trello section as example)
  • Render -- invoked by Documize when raw data needs to be turned into HTML
  • Refresh -- invoked by Documize to get latest copy of raw data (see Trello section as example)

The Markdown section type has a minimal backend footprint:

// Command stub.
func (*Provider) Command(ctx *provider.Context, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	provider.WriteEmpty(w)
}

// Render converts markdown data into HTML suitable for browser rendering.
func (*Provider) Render(ctx *provider.Context, config, data string) string {
	result := blackfriday.Run([]byte(data))

	return string(result)
}

// Refresh just sends back data as-is.
func (*Provider) Refresh(ctx *provider.Context, config, data string) string {
	return data
}

The final step is to register the section type via the section/register.go file:

provider.Register("markdown", &markdown.Provider{Runtime: rt, Store: s})

Please review the code of existing backend implementations:

https://github.com/documize/community/tree/master/domain/section

title: User Interface
body:
The section user interface is divided into two parts and is built using EmberJS.

https://guides.emberjs.com/release

You will need to be familiar with EmberJS and Ember CLI.

Using the Markdown section type as an example, the following files make up the user interface:

  • Rendering the HTML via markdown/type-renderer.hbs and markdown/type-renderer.js
  • Editing the section data via  markdown/type-editor.hbs and markdown/type-editor.js

Each stage like rendering and editing consists of a Javascript file with a .js extension and a HTML file with a .hbs extension. 

The .js and   .hbs files together represent an EmberJS component.

So therefore we have two EmberJS components: 

  • markdown/type-renderer
  • markdown/type-editor

Both these components follow standard EmberJS component lifecycles and design guidelines.

The type-editor component for any section can either be inline or full page.

  • Markdown section type is an example of an inlined editing experience
  • Trello or Jira section types are examples of full page editing experience

CSS declarations for section types should reside in a section-name.scss file like markdown.scss for the Markdown section type. These files use the SASS preprocessor for defining style information. Style information for all section types is linked via all.scss file. 

Please review existing section CSS information:

https://github.com/documize/community/tree/master/gui/app/styles/core/section

Each section type also needs a icon:

  • 30px by 30px png format
  • 60px by 60px (retina version)

Examples of icons for section types:

https://github.com/documize/community/tree/master/gui/public/sections 

The icon filenames match the section type short descriptor (e.g. markdown).
